summary.intent: Establish post-phase-19 performance baselines for the cipher-box API on staging after deployment, and investigate why load test error rates were so high.
summary.outcome: Discovered that someguy's IPNS routing endpoint is completely non-functional (hangs indefinitely on PUT/GET), causing near-100% error rates in load tests. Pivoted to bumping Kubo from v0.34.0 to v0.40.0 locally first; changes committed and pushed to a new branch for local validation before staging deployment.

repo: docker/docker-compose.yml and docker/docker-compose.staging.yml are committed to the repo root but the docker/ directory is also generated/copied during CI deploy — the source of truth for both local and staging compose configs lives in the repo.
The load test harness (vitest) treats SDK-thrown exceptions as metric data points with success:false, not as test failures — tests can 'pass' with 95%+ error rates.
IPNS publish was made fire-and-forget (fire-and-forget delegated routing) in 'fix(api): make delegated routing publish fire-and-forget' — API returns 200 even when someguy times out.
someguy v0.11.1 is actually ahead of the latest stable release (v0.11.0) — no version bump available.
Kubo is 6 minor versions behind: v0.34.0 in use vs v0.40.1 latest. Kubo v0.40 includes specific IPNS reliability fixes.

code.finding: metrics.measure records success:false on thrown exceptions; errors are non-fatal and caught silently, masking high failure rates in test output
Mixed workload uses multiple SDK operations; errors propagate as metrics failures, not test failures
Load test requires LOAD_TEST_API_URL and LOAD_TEST_SECRET env vars; default secret matches staging config

workflow: Running vitest without a precise --testPathPattern can match multiple scenario files (e.g. 'mixed-workload' also matches 'sustained-load'), causing all scenarios to run concurrently and interfere with each other.
Cloudflare 522 errors indicate origin unreachable — can appear when sustained-load tests overwhelm connections, masking whether other tests actually completed.
Verifying IPNS routing directly with curl (with explicit timeout) is a fast way to confirm whether a routing sidecar's IPNS endpoint is functional vs. just accepting connections and hanging.

friction: vitest --testPathPattern='mixed-workload' inadvertently matched 'sustained-load', causing all 5 load test scenarios to run simultaneously and pollute results with 522 Cloudflare errors.
The load test harness reports 'pass' even with 95%+ error rates, making it non-obvious that something is fundamentally broken — required manual log inspection to diagnose.
docker/ directory not being in an obvious location (was in a subdirectory during initial search) caused multiple failed glob/find attempts before locating compose files.
someguy IPNS endpoint hangs indefinitely with no response — difficult to distinguish from slow vs. broken without an explicit timeout test.
Nearly 2000 abort errors accumulated in 10 minutes during load testing before root cause was identified.
open_items: Validate Kubo v0.40.0 works correctly in local dev environment before deploying to staging.
Decide whether to keep someguy (if Kubo upgrade fixes IPNS) or revert DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL to https://delegated-ipfs.dev or remove delegated routing entirely.
Re-run post-phase-19 load test baselines (mixed-workload, ipns-publish-storm) once routing is functional to get comparable metrics vs. phase-18.
Consider fixing the load test harness to fail tests when error rates exceed a threshold, rather than silently recording failures as metrics.
Investigate whether someguy's IPNS routing issue is a known bug or configuration problem — v0.11.1 IPNS PUT/GET completely non-functional despite DHT having 169 peers.
